subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should OpenClaw core own a durable SQLite-backed capacity-wait queue for provider API-limit pauses, and should the existing followup-restart and provider-cooldown PRs be folded into that design?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses provider fallback, session state, message delivery, persistent storage, user-visible waiting status, and replay guarantees, so automation should not choose the product boundary from the partial PRs alone.

options.title: Sponsor A Core Queue Design
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and require a SQLite-backed design that coordinates or supersedes the partial followup and provider-cooldown PRs.

options.title: Narrow To Restart Persistence
options.body: Let a followup-restart PR solve only gateway-restart queue loss and leave provider-limit capacity waiting for separate future work.

options.title: Reject Core Capacity Queueing
options.body: Decide that providers, plugins, or clients should handle capacity waiting outside OpenClaw core orchestration.

recommendation.title: Sponsor A Core Queue Design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and require a SQLite-backed design that coordinates or supersedes the partial followup and provider-cooldown PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across queue/runtime refactors and model fallback paths that this design decision crosses.
